title: Fear Is Not Always Fear: Variation in Emotion Label Equivalence Across Datasets
abstract: arXiv:2610.12841v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Emotion classifiers are routinely applied beyond their training data, on the assumption that same-named labels such as fear or surprise mean the same thing across resources. We test this assumption for five labels shared by GoEmotions, XED, and BRIGHTER, comparing models on identical inputs and under cross-corpus transfer. On the same texts, one fear classifier flags 71% as fearful and another 8%, yet the two largely agree on how the texts rank. Across 30 resource-label comparisons, training-label prevalence explains about half of this kind of scale mismatch, and a fitted intercept removes most of it. What recalibration cannot repair is larger: transferred models lose 55% of native discrimination in aggregate, agreement in ranking between classifiers is only weakly related to that loss, and for surprise the resources disagree about which texts express the emotion. translated_title: 恐惧并不总是恐惧：跨数据集的情感标签等价性差异
translated_abstract: 情感分类器经常被应用于其训练数据之外的场景，其前提假设是诸如“恐惧”或“惊讶”等同名标签在不同资源中具有相同的含义。我们针对GoEmotions、XED和BRIGHTER三个数据集共享的五个标签检验了这一假设，在相同输入以及跨语料库迁移两种条件下对模型进行比较。在相同的文本上，一个恐惧分类器将71%的文本判定为恐惧，而另一个仅判定8%，但两者对文本的恐惧程度排序在很大程度上是一致的。在30项资源-标签比较中，训练标签的分布比例（prevalence）解释了约一半的这种规模不匹配，且通过拟合截距即可消除其中大部分。然而，重新校准无法修复的问题更为严重：迁移后的模型总体损失了55%的原生判别能力，分类器之间的排序一致性仅与该损失呈弱相关，而且对于“惊讶”这一标签，不同资源对哪些文本表达了该情感存在分歧。因此，训练资源的选择可能会改变研究结论。
tldr: 该论文实证表明，GoEmotions、XED和BRIGHTER数据集中同名情感标签（如恐惧、惊讶）的含义并不等价——由标签分布差异导致的规模不匹配可通过校准大幅修复，但模型跨语料迁移会损失约55%的判别能力，因此训练数据的选择会直接改变情感分类的研究结论。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically shows that identically named emotion labels (e.g., fear, surprise) are not equivalent across GoEmotions, XED, and BRIGHTER: while prevalence-driven scale mismatches can be largely fixed by recalibration, cross-corpus transfer costs models about 55% of their native discrimination, meaning the choice of training resource can change downstream conclusions.
